lawyer:
Mr. Sayed Amirul Islam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Mahmuda Begum Advocate-on-record ----- For the petitioners 
Nikhilesh Datta, Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Sufia khatun Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondents

Rafiquunnesa and another ----- Petitioner

full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hasan J.:- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 27.01.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2878 of 1999 discharging the rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 30.06 1999 passed in Title Appeal No. 02 of 19996 by the then learned Subordinate Judge (now joint District Judge) First Court Comilla, allowing the appeal setting said the judgment and decree dated 30.10.19995 passed in Title Sit No. of 1994 by the Assistant Judge, Barura Comilla dismissing the suit on contest. 

 3. Abdur Rahman , the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos. 1-7 as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 86 of 19994 in the Court of Assistant Judge. Barura Comilla impleading the respondents and the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners as the defendants. The plaintiff's cases is the defendant No. 2 being the owner of the suit land sold the same to defendant, No. 1 by a registered deed of sale dated 10.06.1976 and after obtaining certified copy of the document ,the plaintiff being the owner of the contagious land filed Pre-emption case No. 22 of 1976. Pre-emption Case No. 22 of 1976 was subsequently numbered as miscellaneous pre-emption Case No. 41 of 1083 and during the pendency of the pre-emption case. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in collusion with each other filed Title Suit No. 488 of 1977 and obtained a compromise decree to the effect that the deed of sale dated 10.06 1976 which is the subject matter of pre-emption Case No. 22 of 1976 was a "nadabi" deed and not a deed of sale. Title suit No. 488 of 1977 was filed to defeat the right of pre-emption of the plaintiff. Purchaser -respondent No 1 filed written objection in which he did neither disclose the date of the decree nor did he file a copy of the compromise decree with the written objection The deed of sale dated 20.03 19754 executed by defendant No. 2 in favour of defendant No. 1 is out and out a deed of sale and hence the suit has been filled. 

 4. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. His case in short is that Charag Ali Munshi father of the defendant got title and possession of the suit land after obtaining settlement. After that, he died leaving behind four sons and three daughters as heirs and by amicable petition, defendant No. 1 and his brother, Tofazzal got possession in the suit land as well as other land. The defendant stated that during SA operation the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No. 2 and for that reason , defendant No. 2 executed and registered the alleged 'nadabi' deed in favour of defendant No. 1 .The scribe mistakenly wrote the deed of sale in favour of defendant No. 1 .The scribe mistakenly wrote the deed of sale in place of 'nadabi' deed. As such, defendant No. 1 filled title suit no. 487 of 1977 in the Third of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Comilla and defendant Nos. land 2 obtained decree by way, of compromise. Hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. Against the judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 02 of 1996 before the district Judge, Comilla and on transfer, the appeal was hared and disposed of the learned Subordinate Judge Court (now Joint-District Judge) Second court Comilla who by his judgment and order dated 30.061996 allowed the same and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

 7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the appellate Court, the defendants filed a revisional application before the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 2878 of 1999. After hearing the parties the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 27.01.2003 discharged the Rule. 

 9. Mr. Sayed Amirul Islam learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the leave petitioners, submits that respondent No. 2-4 did not have local standi file the instant to file the instant suit and that the High Court division erroneously concurred with the findings of the appellate Court and as such, the impugned it mint should be set aside. He further submits that respondent Nos. 2-4 had the knowledge of filling the suit as it is evident from written objection filled by the leave petitioners and that the suit filed by respondent Nos. 2-4 challenging the compromise decree passed in Title sit No. 288 of 1077 was fraudulent and as such the impugned judgment delivered by the High Court Division should be set aside. 

 13. Plaintiff respondent No. 1 as the pre-emptor filed Pre-emption Case No. 208 of 1976 renumbered as Pre-emption Case No. 40 of 1983 against the deed of sale dated 13.04.1975 registered during the pendency on the aforesaid pre-emption case. Purchaser-respondent No.1 filed Title Suit No. 488 of 1977 on 12.11.1977 praying for declaration that the deed of sale dated 20.03.1975 was a 'nadabi' deed and obtained a compromise decree on 20.01.1977 within a span of 38 days The trial Court did not consider the case of the plaintiff-respondent in its proper perspective and erroneously found that plaintiff-respondent No. 01 had no locus standi to file the suit. The subsequent change of deed of sale into a 'nadabi' deed was done frustrate the right pre-emption. The judgment and decree obtained in Title Suit No. 488 of 1977 was fraudulent Fraud vitiates everything. 

 15. Mr. Sayed Amirul Islam, learned senior Advocate contends that the suit was hopelessly barred by limitation and that the Appellate Court and High Court Division erroneously found that the suit was not barred by limitation. Such a contention is of no avail as limitation would run from the date actual knowledge of the decree passed in Title Suit 488 of 1977 and the suit was filed with the statutory period of limitation as soon as the plaintiff-respondent came to know of the impugned decree. What is important to note here is that the defendant-petitioner did not file the certified copy of the decree with the written objection submitted in the preemption case. A mere case of obtaining a decree in the written objection the suit is not sufficient for reckoning the period of limitation.
